thread:
meera: quick check — canary rollout exposed some clients to intermittent 429s on /v1/generate when traffic spikes. wondering what signal we want SDKs to treat as "soft" vs hard 429 so clients can fallback to the hourly quota or cached response.

alex: saw that in the canary logs, per-route burst exhaustion for the canary pool. we returned 429 + headers, but they look a bit noisy.

sam: what headers did we send? we currently include: `X-Quota-Route: /v1/generate`, `X-Quota-Bucket: route:generate:canary`, `X-Quota-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 3` and a body with `{ "error": "quota_exhausted" }`

meera: ok — question: should `X-Quota-Remaining: 0` + `Retry-After` imply a soft 429 (retry with backoff) or should SDKs treat it as terminal for a short window and immediately fallback to alternate endpoint?

jen: my vote: if `X-Quota-Remaining` is 0 but `Retry-After` <= 5s treat as soft — client should retry with jitter. if `Retry-After` > 30s consider fallback to a non-canary route or to a lower-cost model. also add an explicit `X-Quota-Type: burst` vs `X-Quota-Type: sustained` to disambiguate.

alex: agree re `X-Quota-Type`. also we should add `X-Quota-WindowMs` so clients can calculate smoothing. for example: `X-Quota-WindowMs: 60000` meaning bucket refills every minute.

meera: can we sketch an example response we want from runtime for a burst-exhausted soft signal? I can ship SDK heuristics once we agree.

sam: example payload I'd expect (short):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Quota-Route: /v1/generate
X-Quota-Bucket: route:generate:canary
X-Quota-Type: burst
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-WindowMs: 10000
Retry-After: 3
Content-Type: application/json

{ "error": "quota_exhausted", "hint": "burst_exhausted" }
```

meera: perfect. SDK behavior proposal:
- if X-Quota-Type==burst and Retry-After <= 5s -> retry with exponential backoff starting 200ms + jitter, up to total 2s.
- if X-Quota-Type==sustained or Retry-After > 5s -> attempt immediate fallback: either route-level fallback header `X-Fallback-Route: /v1/generate-legacy` or fall back to cached response.

jen: question about metrics: we need to emit a metric when SDK chooses fallback vs when it retries, so we can tune thresholds. add `client-choice` tag on logs.

alex: also edge-case: sparse bursts from many small clients can appear as sustained exhaustion. runtime should set `X-Quota-Scope: client` vs `X-Quota-Scope: route` to indicate whether the token accounting is per-client or pooled. that will help SDKs decide whether to back off globally or try again quickly.

meera: nice. can we add a short compatibility note for older clients that only look at `Retry-After`? recommend runtime include both `Retry-After` (seconds) and `Retry-After-Ms` for subsecond precision.

sam: done — I'll update the runtime canary to emit these headers: `X-Quota-Type`, `X-Quota-Scope`, `X-Quota-WindowMs`, `Retry-After-Ms`. fallback header `X-Fallback-Route` optional.

jen: one more: for canary vs prod parity, if canary returns fallback header, prod should as well, but maybe with different values. ensure we document in API contract doc.

meera: action items:
- sam: change canary runtime to emit the example headers (ETA today).
- alex: update SDK heuristics PR to treat `burst` vs `sustained` as above and emit telemetry tags (ETA tomorrow).
- jen: add short note in /docs/api-contracts/rate-limits.md about header semantics and backward compatibility (ETA EOD).

rate-limiter-bot: deploy-check: canary runtime change passed unit tests, load tests show transient 429s reduced by 40% when enabling per-client scope. :white_check_mark:

meera: sweet. thanks all — if anyone sees additional weirdness in the next few hours ping here and tag @meera. :thumbsup:
